formalization.document_kind: Architecture and delivery gameplan; no implementation
formalization.purpose: Find bounded counterexamples to declared data-access and transaction policies for an explicitly supported PostgreSQL 16 subset.
formalization.assurance_claim: No counterexample found means only that the modeled property held for the reported finite bounds, environment, semantics profile, and completed checks.
formalization.first_release_mode: Offline/pre-deployment analyzer using synthetic schemas and data; no production SQL execution.
deterministic_pipeline: SQLeanParser Advanced AST / validated typed graph
typed bag-aware relational IR + effect IR
Rust witness validation and structured evidence
formalization.ai_boundary: AI can propose typed edits and explain existing evidence. It cannot decide support, alter formal results, silently weaken policies, or implement SQL/Alloy translation.
formalization.query_semantics: Eval(Q, state, parameters, context) -> Bag<Row> | OrderedRows | SqlError; modeled nondeterminism is explicit.
formalization.transaction_semantics: Step(statement, prestate, context) -> candidate_state, observations, outcome; Exec(transaction) composes steps with commit/abort behavior and exact frame conditions.
formalization.admissibility: A(s,p,c) = well_formed(s,c) AND enforced_database_constraints(s) AND declared_preconditions(s,p,c).
obligations: SAT(A) establishes that assumptions admit an initial state within the selected bounds.
SAT(A AND Exec(T,s,p,c,s2,o)) establishes at least one modeled execution; a missing execution is an encoding/coverage issue unless separately justified.
SAT(A AND Exec(T,s,p,c,s2,o) AND Bad(s,p,c,s2,o)) seeks a counterexample for each named property.
Bad includes committed business-invariant violation, disallowed observed output, disallowed write delta, or an abort classified as unexpected by the declared contract.
Expected error paths are still reported; an error is not automatically a business-invariant violation.
A property under test is never imposed as a poststate fact. Database-enforced constraints determine commit versus abort.
For invariant-preservation checks, require the named business invariant in the prestate as an explicit assumption; finding a pre-existing violation is a separate diagnostic.
formalization.reverse_mapping: RA/effect IR -> canonical parameterized PostgreSQL is deterministic for an admitted fragment. Alloy -> SQL is only a partial decoder for SQLolla-generated, versioned, integrity-checked model packages; arbitrary Alloy specifications have no general SQL inverse.
exclusions_from_claim: Unmodeled triggers, functions, privileges or concurrency
Safety of deployed execution after schema/query/context drift
General confidentiality noninterference; initial read checks cover declared forbidden outputs, with two-execution information-flow modeling reserved for later work.

relational_dsl.representation: A versioned typed JSON AST is the canonical DSL. Low-code blocks and optional human-readable algebra are views over that AST.
scalar_types_initial: BOOL with SQL UNKNOWN in predicates
Opaque TEXT equality under a declared supported comparison profile

operators.phase: M2; Division defined as a set-domain derived operator with explicit empty-domain behavior
M2; exact NULL, empty-group, type and overflow behavior required
M2; sequence semantics and tie nondeterminism, never pretend these are ordinary set RA
M5 research; report depth exhaustion, no general termination claim

nonclassical_semantics: Rows have occurrence identities; projection can create equal-valued duplicates without collapsing them. Alloy's set relations need an explicit occurrence encoding.
SQL equality and boolean operations use TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN. WHERE/HAVING/ON match only TRUE.
Duplicate/grouping equality is distinct from predicate equality; NULLs group together as required by the supported PostgreSQL operation.
Outer joins create explicit null-extended output occurrences.
Scalar subqueries have zero-row NULL, one-row value, and multi-row error outcomes.
Set ALL variants retain multiplicity arithmetic; do not replace EXCEPT ALL by set difference.
Unordered results are bags. ORDER BY ties and LIMIT without a total order require all permitted outcomes or a support diagnostic.
Casts and arithmetic are partial functions with errors. Do not assume expression short-circuit order or hide planner-time failures.
Context-dependent functions require declared context and an admitted semantic model; volatile/effectful functions are unsupported initially.
relational_dsl.normalization: Only apply rewrites with stated bag/NULL/error/collation preconditions. Disable optimizer-style rewrites by default until independently checked.
relational_dsl.sql_emission: Quote resolved identifiers, emit typed parameters separately, preserve positional output schema and parameter maps, and reparse/rebind generated SQL. Check normalize(lower(parse(emit(IR)))) = normalize(IR) for the admitted fragment, and separately validate semantics; this equality does not establish execution equivalence.

envelope: statements as individually parsed SQL strings
effects_and_transactions.parsing_boundary: Use structured boundaries because SQLeanParser's typed AST does not parse transaction control. Never split arbitrary SQL on semicolons.
effects_and_transactions.initial_profile: Single transaction with no concurrent transactions; this is not a claim about default PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED behavior under concurrency.
state_model: Table row identities and typed values
Direct and modeled indirect change sets
transition_rules: All UPDATE assignment expressions read the appropriate old row; preserve untouched rows, columns and tables.
INSERT allocates fresh row identities and checks capacity; DELETE removes exactly selected rows before modeled referential actions.
Each statement uses explicit snapshot semantics and read-your-writes in the sequential profile.
Enforced NOT NULL, PK/UNIQUE and supported CHECK/FK constraints cause commit or abort as PostgreSQL does; CHECK UNKNOWN does not by itself reject a row.
Rollback restores modeled transactional table state. Previously observed data is not erased by rollback.
Immediate and deferred constraints are distinct; deferred constraints, sequences, triggers and cascades stay unsupported until their transitions are implemented.
Expected SQL errors and unintended persistent changes are separate findings.

After an error, model PostgreSQL's failed-transaction behavior and eventual rollback; do not continue applying subsequent writes as though the statement succeeded. Savepoints and recovery inside an aborted transaction are unsupported initially.
catalog_requirements: Absence or modeled presence of each effect dependency
effects_and_transactions.absent_metadata: A declared synthetic catalog may assert a closed effect universe. A real catalog import must establish relevant metadata completeness; unknown is not equivalent to absent.

later_concurrency_profile.boundary: Validate each isolation model against PostgreSQL 16 schedules; sequential checking alone cannot justify a concurrency claim. Client retry logic must be modeled to claim retry safety.

effects_and_transactions.parameter_contract: Parameters are local to each statement; $1 in one statement is not implicitly the same binding in another. MVP bindings are explicit typed inputs. Feed-forward from earlier results requires a later explicit, typed binding node; no hidden application control flow.
effects_and_transactions.context_contract: Capture session, statement and transaction context explicitly. Time-dependent expressions remain unsupported until transaction/statement-time semantics are defined.
effects_and_transactions.row_accounting: Track matched/affected rows, value-changed rows, inserted/deleted rows and returned rows separately. An UPDATE assigning existing values may still count as affected.

solver_and_validation.initial_backend: Alloy 6.2 via Java17, preferring a bundled pure-Java SAT solver such as SAT4J after feasibility verification; benchmark native solvers later.
bounds_policy: Never use arbitrary small intermediate scopes that can suppress cross-products or INSERT rows.
Compute conservative capacities or use a structurally complete occurrence encoding; scope exhaustion yields INCONCLUSIVE.
Small Alloy integers are analysis bounds, not PostgreSQL machine integer semantics.
Guard all arithmetic and cardinality encodings against solver overflow; model SQL overflow as an explicit outcome where supported.
Start with exact finite semantics. Approximation requires a documented soundness direction; candidate counterexamples need concretization and no-counterexample claims require adequate soundness.
Increase scopes in a declared ladder; reports show completed checks and skipped/timed-out scopes separately.

proposed_demo_budget.status: Initial targets to benchmark, not measured capacity; preflight must refuse unsupported model sizes.

witness_processing: Decode typed rows and parameter values
Recompute outcome with independent Rust interpreter
Attempt witness reduction with bounded additional queries; call the result reduced unless minimality is actually established.
Replay in disposable PostgreSQL16 instance where permitted
Compare output multiplicities, changes, errors and transaction outcome
solver_and_validation.determinism_contract: Equal canonical inputs and pinned compiler versions yield byte-identical IR/model/SQL and stable identifiers. SAT witness selection can vary across solvers/platforms; archive the concrete witness and options instead of promising identical solutions.
solver_and_validation.replay_safety: Only isolated disposable databases with synthetic data and restricted roles; no production replay and no untrusted effectful SQL.
corpus_strategy: Import existing synthetic and source-derived fixtures unchanged with origin, commit, license and hashes.
Separate syntax-only inputs from schema-complete semantic cases; never invent an application catalog and label it authentic.
Keep external templates unexpanded unless a separately modeled expansion is supplied.
Add generated finite schemas/instances and boundary values for each admitted operator.
Differentially compare PostgreSQL16, the Rust interpreter and Alloy witnesses; expected output comes from independently reviewed contracts.
Use meaningful metamorphic checks only under their valid SQL bag/NULL/error preconditions.
Mutation-test the encoder by dropping filters, frame constraints, NULL rules, parameter bindings and tenant predicates; reviewers must detect seeded defects.
Report exact denominators and all unsupported cases; upstream parse totals are not SQLolla proof coverage.
Provide a pinned disposable PostgreSQL16 runtime in the later test environment (WSL/Ubuntu or containers locally). Its availability was not established by the supplied dependency list.

Exhaustively compare all permitted outcomes on tiny finite domains, including successful commits, aborts, output bags and allowed nondeterminism. Replaying only found witnesses cannot detect outcomes omitted by a faulty encoding.

byot_and_ai.normalization: Each adapter handles its actual authentication, streaming, tool-call and structured-output protocol; compatibility is not assumed to mean identical APIs. Pin supported API versions and model capabilities; fail visibly for unsupported features. Link current provider data/retention terms rather than promising universal no-retention behavior.
credential_custody: Browser form necessarily receives the key transiently; send over TLS to the Rust service and clear the input.
Keep credentials in a short-lived session secret store in memory by default; never localStorage, URLs, analytics, logs, evidence files or agent checkpoints.
Hosted mode discloses that Cloudflare may terminate TLS and the hosted origin processes the key. Private mode can bypass Cloudflare.
Use revocable session references, disconnect/expiry deletion and best-effort memory zeroization; do not promise instantaneous erasure from every runtime/network buffer.
Persistent vault/KMS integration is a later explicit deployment option.
egress_controls: Known provider allowlist in hosted mode
Custom endpoints only through administrator policy
No redirects carrying credentials across origins
DNS rebinding and private/loopback/link-local/metadata address protections
Timeout, size, rate, token and spend caps
byot_and_ai.data_sharing: Default to synthetic/redacted evidence. Show the exact outbound payload and obtain explicit sharing consent before sending sensitive schema, SQL or witness content.
pipeline: Revise with bounded loop or stop
byot_and_ai.langgraph_like_design: Implement an explicit typed state machine/DAG with checkpoints in Rust. LangGraph-like orchestration does not require adding a Python backend or placing trust in LLM tool output.
agent_limits: Cannot reduce scope, remove policies or change verdict without an explicit visible user change
Resume never repeats a mutation implicitly
byot_and_ai.explanation_validation: Require valid evidence references and keep formal verdict immutable. Structured-output validation cannot prove the prose true; unsupported claims are labeled or replaced by deterministic templates.
byot_and_ai.availability: All formal analysis, finding summaries and demo flows work without a token or provider availability.
byot_and_ai.injection_boundary: SQL comments, identifiers, schema descriptions and retrieved text are untrusted data; never instructions with authority to change policies, tools or credentials.
web_security: Sanitize AI Markdown and disallow raw HTML
Restrictive CSP and no third-party analytics on token entry surfaces
Secret handles are tenant/session-bound and never authorize by possession alone

release_acceptance: All eight requirements have corresponding design decisions and owned delivery gates.
Every advertised operator/type/effect has explicit semantics, capability entries and independent behavioral checks.
No open critical/high finding that can produce false assurance, secret disclosure or cross-tenant access.
Every curated positive demo defect yields a validated witness; every repaired demo has satisfiable assumptions and a completed bounded result.
Mutation suite detects seeded loss of tenant filters, frame constraints, duplicate/NULL behavior and parameter identity.
Timeout, cancellation, unsupported syntax, incomplete catalog and inconsistent assumptions remain distinguishable in API/UI/evidence.
Canonical inputs produce reproducible compiler artifacts across supported platforms; witness variability is tracked separately.
BYOT disabled/provider failure leaves formal analysis usable; credential deletion and storage/logging checks pass.
All supported deployment targets pass isolated install/run/cancel/error/offline checks and documented recovery.
Alloy/Rust/PostgreSQL discrepancies block the affected capability rather than being explained away by AI.
